name: update_sandbox
description:
Update a named sandbox's configuration, such as resources, runtime, timeout, persistence, snapshot retention, or network policy. Only provided fields change. With resume=true, a stopped sandbox is resumed by creating a new instance from its snapshot.

CLI fallback on MCP failure (partial): vercel api /v2/sandboxes/{name} --method PATCH. Fill placeholders from inputs.

projectId.description: The project ID that owns the named sandbox. When provided, takes precedence over OIDC project context.

currentSnapshotId.description: The snapshot ID to set as the current snapshot. Must be active and belong to the same project.

env.description: Default environment variables for the sandbox. Set to empty object to clear.

failoverRegions.description: The regions the sandbox falls back to when it cannot be created in `region`.

keepLastSnapshots.description: Protect the N most recent snapshots with different expiration/deletion behavior. Set to null to clear.

count.description: Number of most recent snapshots to keep.

deleteEvicted.description: Whether to immediately delete evicted snapshots. Defaults to true.

expiration.description: Expiration time in milliseconds for kept snapshots. Falls back to snapshotExpiration.

drive.description: Name of the drive to mount. The drive must already exist.

mode.description: Mount the drive as read-write, or as a read-only snapshot. One writer is permitted at a time.

mounts.description: Drives to mount to the sandbox at the provided path. Replaces the current mounts; an empty object removes them all. Changes take effect when the next session starts.

networkId.description: The Connect network id for the target Secure Compute private network. Set to null to remove the sandbox from Secure Compute.

oneOf.description: Network access policy for the sandbox.\n    Controls which external hosts the sandbox can communicate with.\n    Use \"allow-all\" mode to allow all traffic, \"deny-all\" to block all traffic or \"custom\" to provide specific rules.

allowedCIDRs.description: List of IP address ranges (in CIDR notation) the sandbox is allowed to connect to. Traffic to these addresses bypasses domain-based restrictions.

items.description: An IPv4 address range in CIDR notation (e.g., \"35.192.0.0/12\").

allowedDomains.description: List of domain names the sandbox is allowed to connect to. Only applies when mode is \"custom\". Supports wildcard patterns (e.g., \"*.example.com\" matches all subdomains).

items.description: A domain name pattern. Use \"*\" for wildcard matching of subdomains (e.g., \"*.example.com\").

deniedCIDRs.description: List of IP address ranges (in CIDR notation) the sandbox is blocked from connecting to. These rules take precedence over all allowed rules.

items.description: An IP address range in CIDR notation to block.

injectionRules.description: HTTP header injection rules for outgoing requests matching specific domains. Traffic to matching domains will be intercepted instead of proxied through encrypted connections.

domain.description: The domain (or pattern) of requests to add headers for. Supports wildcards like *.example.com.

headers.description: HTTP headers to inject into requests for this domain. Existing headers with the same name will be overridden.

match.description: Optional L7 match. When provided, the injection rule only applies to requests that satisfy every specified dimension. When multiple injection rules target the same domain they are evaluated in order and the first match wins; a rule without `match` matches any request and shadows later rules for the same domain.

key.description: Matcher for the entry key (header name or query key).

response.description: Answer matching requests from the proxy with this response instead of forwarding them to the origin. Combine with a `match` on an earlier rule to allow one sub-path and reject the rest of a domain.

contentType.description: Value of the `Content-Type` response header. Required when `body` is set.

headers.description: HTTP response headers. Framing and hop-by-hop headers are managed by the proxy and cannot be set.

statusCode.description: HTTP status code returned to the sandbox.

oneOf.description: A rule applied to requests matching a domain in the network policy. Only one of `transform`, `forwardURL`, or `response` can be specified per rule.

persistent.description: Whether the sandbox persists its state across restarts via automatic snapshots.

ports.description: List of ports to expose from the sandbox. Each port will be accessible via a unique URL. Maximum of 15 ports can be exposed.

items.description: A port number to expose from the sandbox. Must be between 1024 and 65535.

region.description: The Vercel region in which to create the sandbox.

memory.description: The amount of memory in megabytes to allocate to the sandbox. Must equal vcpus * 2048.

vcpus.description: The number of virtual CPUs to allocate to the sandbox. Must be 1, or an even number.

runtime.description: The runtime environment for the sandbox. Determines the pre-installed language runtimes and tools available.

snapshotExpiration.description: Default snapshot expiration time in milliseconds. Set to 0 to disable expiration. When set, this value is used as the default expiration for all snapshots created for this sandbox.

tags.description: Key-value tags to associate with the sandbox. Replaces existing tags. Set to empty object to clear. Maximum 5 tags.

timeout.description: Maximum duration in milliseconds that the sandbox can run before being automatically stopped.

resume.description: Whether to automatically resume a stopped named sandbox by creating a new instance from its snapshot. Defaults to false.

slug.description: Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.

teamId.description: Team ID to use for this operation.
